meta.title: Women's rights
meta.question: Should women and men have the same roles at home, at work and in politics?
meta.measure: Average position on women's roles and rights, from 0 (equality) to 10 (traditional roles)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on women in politics, at work and at home and on measures to increase their representation, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Being a housewife is just as fulfilling as working for pay
When jobs are scarce, men should have more right to a job than women (agree / neither / disagree)
items.notes: European Values Study 1990, 1999, 2008 (3 surveys). The ESS and WVS ask the same statement.

items.wording: A pre-school child is likely to suffer if his or her mother works
items.notes: European Values Study 1990, 1999, 2008 (3 surveys). 2017 drops 'pre-school' and is EVS_CHILD_SUFFERS17.

items.wording: A job is all right, but what most women really want is a home and children
A working mother can establish just as warm and secure a relationship with her children as a mother who does not work
items.notes: European Values Study 1990, 1999, 2008 (3 surveys). 1999's five-point copy (_5c) fails the label check and is not used.

items.wording: Agree or disagree: women should take care of the house
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, January 1991 and March 2000 (2 surveys).

items.wording: It is much better for everyone if the man is the achiever outside the home and the woman takes care of the home and family (agree-disagree)
Women should take care of running their homes and leave running the country up to men (agree-disagree)
A preschool child is likely to suffer if his or her mother works (agree-disagree)
It is more important for a wife to help her husband's career than to have one herself (agree-disagree)

A working mother can establish just as warm a relationship with her children as a mother who does not work (agree-disagree)
Should steps be taken to increase women's participation in public life (1997) / in politics (2010), since women have fewer opportunities?
items.notes: CBOS 1997-01 and 2010-08 (2 surveys). 'Public life' in 1997, 'politics' in 2010.

items.wording: Should more, the same number or fewer women than now hold leading posts in the government?
items.notes: CBOS 1997-01, 1999-11, 2006-08, 2013-02 (4 surveys). The other posts in the battery (parties, administration, firms, courts) are left out as redundant.

items.wording: When jobs are scarce, men should have more right to a job than women (agree / neither / disagree)
items.notes: World Values Survey 1997, 2005, 2012 (3 usable surveys). The 1989 wave falls before CAL_START (January 1990) and is left out by the pipeline.
